title: Gate VCF Operations adapter onboarding behind the connection precheck
prompt:
Implement `Register-VcfOpsAdapterInstance` in `src/VcfOps.AdapterOnboarding/VcfOps.AdapterOnboarding.psm1`. That file is the only one you may edit. Build the function on the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI SDK module that the environment already provides: use its cmdlets for the session and for every API call. Do not vendor, copy or reimplement the SDK, do not add another dependency, and do not hand-roll HTTP requests.

Before implementing, research the VCF Operations `acquireToken`, `getCurrentVersionOfServer`, `testConnection`, `createAdapterInstance`, and `releaseToken` operations and their generated VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 bindings in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. Use only those five operationIds. The service base path is `/suite-api`, and the token issued by `acquireToken` is presented as an `Authorization` header with the `OpsToken` prefix.

Onboarding an adapter instance must be gated by the platform's own connection precheck. Run `testConnection` first with the requested adapter settings and credential. Only when it succeeds may you issue the mutating `createAdapterInstance` call. A new inline credential is persisted by `testConnection`; preserve every adapter setting in the create request but replace the inline credential fields with the `credentialInstanceId` returned by the precheck. Re-sending the secret-bearing credential makes the live create fail with HTTP 422. Preserve a caller-supplied existing credential ID. When the precheck fails, no request may reach the adapter-instance collection, although the precheck may already have persisted a new inline credential: do not retry it, do not fall back to creating the instance, and do not attempt the create and delete it afterwards. Send `createAdapterInstance` with `force=false` so the server-side gate agrees with yours, and leave the unset `extractIdentifierDefaults` query member off the request entirely. Release the session on the way out along both paths.

Preserve the supplied parameter block exactly. `Server`, `Port`, `Credential`, `Name`, `AdapterKindKey`, `AdapterCredentialName`, and `AdapterCredentialKindKey` are mandatory; `Protocol` defaults to `https`, `AuthSource` defaults to `local`, and `AdapterCredentialId`, `AdapterCredentialField`, `Description`, `CollectorId`, `MonitoringInterval`, `ResourceIdentifier`, and `SkipCertificateCheck` are optional. Supply exactly one of an existing `AdapterCredentialId` or a nonempty ordered `AdapterCredentialField` map. The credential uses the adapter's `AdapterKindKey`; inline fields become ordered name/value pairs. `ResourceIdentifier` is an ordered dictionary of identifier name to value that becomes the payload's `resourceIdentifiers` array of bare name/value pairs, preserving the caller's order. `SkipCertificateCheck` tolerates an untrusted server certificate.

Return a single object carrying `Status`, `PrecheckPassed`, `AdapterInstanceId` and `Message`. A successful onboarding returns `Status` `Created`, `PrecheckPassed` true and the identifier from the `createAdapterInstance` response. A rejected precheck is a reported outcome, not an exception: return `Status` `PrecheckFailed`, `PrecheckPassed` false, an empty `AdapterInstanceId`, and the diagnostic the platform returned in `Message`.

Honor the exact wire contract. Every optional member the caller did not supply must be omitted from the JSON body rather than sent empty: omission means the member is absent, never null, a blank string, a zero, or an empty array. A minimal request therefore carries `adapterKindKey`, `name`, and the required `credential`; the precheck credential carries inline `fields`, while create carries its returned `id` and omits those fields. `collectorId` is a string, and `monitoringInterval` is a JSON number; a caller-supplied zero is valid and must not be mistaken for an unset value.

Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Invoke-Verification.ps1`. Verification checks the preserved command signature and SDK-only implementation across a minimal onboarding, a fully specified one, and a rejected precheck. It verifies operation sequence, raw request targets and query members, header values, exact body key sets and values, preservation of adapter settings across the precheck-to-create credential transition, no mutation after a rejected precheck, session release, and omission of every unset optional field.
scenario: A minimal onboarding and a fully specified onboarding each run testConnection before createAdapterInstance with a byte-identical payload, while a rejected precheck stops the workflow so no request reaches the adapter-instance collection.
